original_test_intent: Create a Redfish account, while the preserved source Procedure actually reads an unrelated account certificate resource.
original_method: After resolving the source conflict, create exactly one approved unique temporary account through AccountService/Accounts using least privilege and secret-safe injection, verify identity/role, then delete it and prove the account inventory returns to baseline.
manual_activity: Resolve certificate GET versus account creation, approve the unique temporary username, least-privilege role, secret lifecycle, test duration and cleanup/recovery; never accept Administrator by default.
required_inputs: Secret-provider handles for admin and new password
safety_requirements: Never claim creation coverage from the certificate GET

Create one unique temporary account only
No blind retry after ambiguous creation
Delete or disable through approved cleanup and prove absence
agent_execution_scope: Capture redacted account baseline and slot capacity
Validate username uniqueness, role and password policy
Resolve created member and verify exact identity/role
Audit secret exposure and preserved security logs
engineer_actions: Approve temporary username, least-privilege role, secret handling and lifetime

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: POST /AccountService/Accounts aligns with the title, but it overrides the copied Master Procedure and is unsafe with Administrator default and password interpolation in visible command text; account cleanup is not optional.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After approval, inject the username/password through a non-disclosing secret mechanism, POST one least-privilege account, verify identity/role, then delete it and prove baseline restoration; inspect state before any retry.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 15/10 timing and account-creation identity remain; no username, password, role, account slot or deletion semantics is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat the test as a temporary credential lifecycle with explicit least privilege, non-disclosure and a baseline-to-baseline transaction.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces the unrelated certificate read while preserving the conflict, removes Administrator default/visible password, and adds capacity, ambiguity, delete and secret-exposure audits.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers one temporary account lifecycle only; it does not test existing account modification, broad role policy or certificate resources.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A successful create followed by failed response can leave a residual credential; deletion does not remediate a password disclosed in process or evidence, which requires immediate rotation and incident handling.

project_override_considerations: If project policy requires an Administrator test account, that exceptional privilege must be explicitly approved with an isolated identity and shortest lifetime; it cannot be inferred from DeepSeek's payload. Prefer a dedicated test role when supported.
expected_evidence: Recorded Accounts Creation versus certificate GET conflict
Account schema, role/password policy and slot-capacity result
DELETE status and post-cleanup inventory matching baseline
Unchanged existing accounts/roles/configuration and preserved logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Items and Script identify account creation, but the Master Procedure performs a GET on an account certificate resource. They have different targets, methods and effects, so the conflict must remain explicit while any creation workflow requires separate approval.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The account schema, identity, role, secret provider, approval and cleanup are identifiable prerequisites, making this REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Prevents an unrelated certificate GET from falsely satisfying account creation and replaces a visible Administrator credential POST with a least-privilege, secret-safe, fully cleaned-up account lifecycle.
independent_technical_reasoning: Account creation changes the BMC's authentication surface and persists beyond the test unless cleanup succeeds. The preserved Procedure cannot exercise this purpose at all, while DeepSeek's correction introduces an overprivileged default and risks exposing the password in process arguments and logs. A valid test must start from a hashed/redacted inventory, prove the name is unique and capacity exists, create once, resolve ambiguous responses by listing accounts rather than retrying, and remove the exact created identity. Final evidence must demonstrate both baseline restoration and absence of secret disclosure; hardware PASS remains user-owned.
